data.title: Swiss Bitcoin Payment Platform Takes Servers Offline After Suspected Internal Breach
data.description:
A Swiss Bitcoin (BTC) payment firm has taken its servers offline as a precaution after a malicious user likely reached internal systems and may have seen customer data.

Neuchâtel-based Swiss Bitcoin Pay, which processes on-chain and Lightning payments for merchants, shut the platform down while it investigates.

In an X post, the company says attackers may have accessed customer email addresses, Bitcoin addresses and IBANs, transaction history, and hashed passwords, and that it is not yet clear whether anything else was reached.

“A malicious user has likely gained access to Swiss Bitcoin Pay’s internal systems. As a precaution, we are temporarily shutting down our servers while we investigate and secure our infrastructure… User funds are safe, and any amounts owed to users will be fully returned.”

The firm says that any payments on its platform go straight to merchants’ wallets, and that any amounts owed will be returned in full.

It remains unclear when the service will be made available again as the firm continues to work to ensure its systems are secure.

“We do not have a reopening date yet, but we are working as quickly as possible to secure everything properly.”

Swiss Bitcoin Pay was founded in late 2022 and operates as a non-custodial Bitcoin payment processor.

data.title: Iowa to Hand $25,000,000 to Residents Harmed by Meta in First Consumer Restitution Fund
data.description:
Iowa is setting up the first-of-its-kind restitution fund to hand out $25 million to residents hurt by Meta’s practices aimed at children.

Attorney General Brenna Bird says the state will use $25 million from its $126 million Meta settlement to pay eligible Facebook and Instagram users. Iowa is the first state in the deal to create a consumer fund.

Bird says half of the settlement, about $68 million, must address the harms that prompted the lawsuit.

Says Bird,

“The Meta settlement was a victory for Iowa’s families. Our kids will now be safer online… I’m happy to announce we are the first state to create a fund to share the settlement with Iowans who have been affected by Meta’s bad behavior.”

Other pots include $11 million for the Iowa Kids and Consumers Defense Fund, $10 million in school grants, $10 million for victim support and a Special Victims Unit, $3 million for technology upgrades and about $7.3 million for the Ensuring Child Safety Online Fund.

Roughly $49 million goes to the state’s general fund after legal fees.

Eligibility rules and the claims process will be announced later.

Iowa’s settlement proceeds is the state’s share of the landmark settlement with Meta reached in August when the tech giant agreed to pay a coalition of states at least $12.1 billion.

data.title: Georgia Adviser Steals Nearly $10,000,000 From Elderly Client in Wire Fraud Scheme
data.description:
A former investment adviser will serve more than seven years in prison after stealing nearly $10 million from an elderly client by moving cash into secret accounts.

Ejiroghene Okuma, 44, a Georgia resident, was appointed executor of the estate of the victim’s sister in 2022 and told the victim her estate needed funds, reports Atlanta News First.

The victim allowed him to transfer cash for the sister’s estate. However, Okuma instead transferred the money into bank and brokerage accounts that the client did not know about.

Prosecutors say that Okuma used the stolen money to buy a house in Georgia worth more than $5 million, pay for a beach club membership worth $1.4 million and make roughly $340,000 in church donations.

Okuma pleaded guilty to one count of wire fraud in March. He has just been sentenced to seven years and four months in prison plus three years of supervised release.

U.S. Attorney Theodore Hertzberg says the case should warn fiduciaries who exploit vulnerable clients for personal gain.

“Under the guise of acting as a financial adviser, Okuma abused the trust placed in him by an elderly client… His sentence should send a clear message to fiduciaries who may be tempted to steal: we will seek lengthy prison sentences to punish those who exploit vulnerable citizens to line their own pockets.”

A later hearing will set restitution.

data.title: 17 State Attorneys General Put the Clarity Act in Their Crosshairs After Senators Release New Version of Crypto Bill
data.description:
A group of bipartisan state attorneys general is wading into the Clarity Act debate as the Senate prepares for an upcoming procedural vote on the controversial crypto market structure legislation.

U.S. Senate Banking Digital Assets Subcommittee Chair Cynthia Lummis (R-WY) released the latest version of the Clarity Act on Sunday, outlining “126 Democrat wins” she says were successfully negotiated by her rival party.

Among those “wins” is a ban on federal elected officials, senior executive branch employees and federal judges from issuing or sponsoring a digital asset or maintaining a significant financial interest in an issuer of crypto assets.

That potential regulation is a direct shot at President Donald Trump’s controversial “TRUMP” memecoin, but Lummis notes that Trump himself signed off on the new language.

The new version hasn’t won over all detractors, however: On Monday, a group of attorneys general from 17 states and the District of Columbia penned a letter to Senate Banking Committee Chairman Tim Scott (R-South Carolina) arguing the current iteration of the bill doesn’t do enough to protect crypto investors from scams and fraud.

“While the current draft of the CLARITY Act reserves certain powers for states to prosecute fraud, the language is often ambiguous, unclear, or confined in ways that either create the opportunity to challenge state police powers or outright deprive the states of their ability to continue to combat the scam epidemic. Even though states will prevail in enforcing laws that are not preempted, the benefit of litigation and delay caused by ambiguity accrues to bad actors.”

The bill would largely place the digital assets under the regulatory purview of the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), an agency industry stakeholders believe is friendlier to the sector than the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC).

The potential legislation has faced opposition from traditional financial giants and banking associations, who have argued the bill could put financial stability at risk and cause bank deposits to lose ground to stablecoins.

A procedural vote on the Clarity Act is scheduled for Tuesday; it requires 60 votes and would allow the Senate to debate and consider the legislation in an actual vote.

Polymarket bettors’ confidence in the Clarity Act’s chances of passing this year has mildly improved this week, with its odds jumping from 17% seven days ago to 26% at time of writing.

data.title: Revolut Attackers Leak Customer Data, Demand Daily Payments
data.description:
Threat actors who targeted Revolut are now publicly posting sensitive customer data and threatening to release more every day unless the fintech pays up.

The threat actors say they initially contacted the company with information demands before beginning to share details including those of prominent clients.

They are also promising to release more messages, operational insights and internal data in the coming days.

The group accuses Revolut of negligence around privacy protections and of sharing sensitive information with countries outside its jurisdiction.

They say they’ll release more messages, data and insights into how the Revolut team operates, accusing Revolut of handing over sensitive information to countries outside its jurisdiction.

They accuse the company of negligence around privacy and the exposure of sensitive information.

data.title: DOJ Strike Force Seizes Illicit Marketplace and Restrains $52,000,000 in Crypto
data.description:
Federal authorities are dismantling a major illicit online marketplace used by scammers and restraining $52 million in cryptocurrency assets.

The U.S. Department of Justice says the action forms part of an ongoing effort by a dedicated Strike Force targeting scam centers.

In a related move during the same period another team supported local authorities in Madagascar to shut down 13 Chinese-run scam compounds.

This development extends a broader crackdown that originally focused on Southeast Asia into new regions.

The seizures highlight intensified efforts to disrupt networks behind fraudulent schemes that often target victims worldwide.

Officials are emphasizing the international scope of these operations which aim to dismantle the infrastructure supporting large-scale scams.

The restrained funds represent significant assets tied to the illicit marketplace.

Details of the actions were outlined in official Department of Justice announcements.

The full scope of the seizures and takedowns underscores the growing reach of enforcement against cyber-enabled fraud.

data.title: Solana Mobile Suspends Marketing Email Account After Unauthorized Access
data.description:
A cryptocurrency phone maker is warning customers after suspending its third-party marketing email account over unauthorized access.

Solana Mobile says the access happened during a wider security incident at email provider Brevo.

The incident is part of a larger breach at Brevo that affected 138 customer accounts through a Security Assertion Markup Language Single Sign-On (SAML SSO) vulnerability.

Says Solana Mobile,

“Our third-party marketing email provider, Brevo, experienced a security incident affecting some customer accounts, including Solana Mobile. We identified unauthorized access to our Brevo account, disabled the account, and are working with Brevo to understand the scope of information accessed. To our knowledge, no emails were sent from the Solana Mobile account, but we are continuing to verify with Brevo. A reminder that Solana Mobile will never ask for your seed phrase, private keys, or wallet recovery details.”

Solana Mobile builds crypto-focused smartphones for the Solana ecosystem.

Meanwhile, Brevo says that a handful of customer accounts were used for malicious purposes.

“Six of those accounts were used to send phishing emails to the contacts stored there, and for 43 accounts, they exported the contacts. 93 accounts have no meaningful activity.

The attacker no longer has access…

These messages were sent through legitimate infrastructure, so they passed the usual email authentication checks and looked genuine.

We’ve disabled all links in those emails, but as a preventive measure, please do not click them.

Customers trust us with access to their audiences, and in this case we failed to protect it.”

data.title: AI Boom Driving ‘Astronomical’ Profit Growth, Lifting Information Technology, Energy and Two Other S&P 500 Sectors
data.description:
Powerful demand for artificial intelligence technologies is lifting earnings expectations for companies in the S&P 500.

Analysts now project full-year profit growth of 32% in 2026, a significant increase from the 24% anticipated prior to the latest reporting period, says The Kobeissi Letter.

This quarter saw 86% of S&P 500 firms surpass analyst targets, marking the highest beat rate in half a decade.

Communication Services earnings estimates jumped to 51% growth from the expected 26% at the start of the second quarter, while Consumer Discretionary forecasts rose to 32% from 12%, driven by Amazon’s (AMZN) results.

Energy and information technology sectors now face projections of 83% and 59% growth, respectively, reflecting broad gains from AI infrastructure spending.

“AI is driving astronomical profit growth.”

The Kobeissi Letter highlights that AI is now “single-handedly carrying the global economy.”

“The fact that the S&P 500 is 2.5% away from a record high despite the bond market looking like this is remarkable.

Without AI, the S&P 500 would be at least 50% lower right now.

Without the surge in oil prices, the S&P 500 would be above 9,000.”

Looking closer at artificial intelligence, The Kobeissi Letter predicts the agentic AI market is poised to witness massive growth.

“The enterprise agentic AI market is now expected to grow from $2.6 billion to $24.5 billion by 2030, increasing more than 9x.

These systems can effectively reason and execute with minimal human oversight.

By 2028, 30% of enterprise applications are expected to embed autonomous agents, per Gartner forecasts.

Adoption is expected to expand across customer service, operations, finance, HR, and cybersecurity.

The biggest shift is that AI is moving from simply assisting humans to actually executing and orchestrating work.

This could materially reduce operating costs and improve operational efficiency.

Agentic AI is a major catalyst for corporate efficiency.”

data.title: Bank of America, Goldman Sachs, HSBC and More Raising Brent Oil Price Forecasts Amid Persistent Gulf Shipping Disruptions
data.description:
Major banks are raising their Brent crude oil price forecasts in response to persistent shipping disruptions in the Middle East.

The Frankfurt-based Commerzbank lifted its year-end Brent forecast to $85 per barrel from $75, reports EnergyNow.com.

Goldman Sachs increased its Brent and West Texas Intermediate (WTI) forecasts by $5 a barrel for December 2026 and 2027, expecting the disruptions to last into next year. The bank predicted that Brent could trade at $85 a barrel and WTI at $80 in December, warning that Brent could shatter $120 if Gulf production and exports remain significantly constrained.

Meanwhile, HSBC raised its 2026 Brent forecast to $90 per barrel and its 2027 forecast to $85 per barrel. The bank highlighted the ongoing situation in the Strait of Hormuz, where about 20% of the world’s traded petroleum passes through.

“We think the market is adjusting to a disrupted ‘new normal’ in which the strait is neither fully closed nor fully open, but persistently impaired.”

Bank of America raised its Brent forecast to $83 per barrel for the second half of this year and $75 for 2027. Bank of America outlined further risks.

“More disruptions could push it toward $120/bbl, while vast energy infra damage could drive prices to $150/bbl.”

Oil prices ended the week above $100 per barrel for the first time since mid-May, with US diesel prices hitting a record high.

data.title: Alleged Scammers Drain $270,000+ From Michigan Senior in Fake FTC Email Scam
data.description:
A Michigan senior has lost more than $270,000 from pension accounts after scammers posing as federal agents pushed her to buy gold and hand it over.

The 70-year-old Hazel Park resident got an unsolicited email that claimed to come from the Federal Trade Commission and falsely tied her to a vehicle with a dead body and drugs, reports CBS News.

Says Hazel Park Police Department Detective Chad Jackson,

“She received an email that said she had a warrant for her arrest. Claimed it was from the Federal Trade Commission. They said that there was a car found that had a dead body in it, and there was drugs involved, and her name was attached to it, and her information was in the vehicle.”

She contacted a supposed agent who told her to pay money and buy gold so she could wipe out the fabricated charges.

The caller warned her not to contact local authorities and said the funds would come back after a holding period.

Adds Jackson,

“They threatened her that she shouldn’t call the police locally because there is a warrant, so they would probably arrest her, and they could handle it separately outside of that. She was told that her money would be held for a period of time to clear her name and that they would return it back to her account. But her money never returned, so weeks later she contacted us.”

Further demands pushed her to liquidate both her pension and her late husband’s, for more than $270,000.

Investigators later used community Flock camera recordings to track 30-year-old Ranjeet Singh from Sacramento.

Authorities extradited the suspect to Michigan and arraigned him on two counts of false pretenses with a $300,000 bond.
